thread.title: What This Market Needs to Do to Get Back on Track

title: What This Market Needs to Do to Get Back on Track
text:
What This Market Needs to Do to Get Back on Track By gs 
The week started on a high note as Netflix ( NFLX ) reported strong earnings on Monday night and popped the S&P 500 out of its recent trading range. The stock closed above its 50-day simple moving average for the first time in over a month. 
Hopes were high that this would lead to an upbeat earnings season but then IBM ( IBM ) disappointed, Goldman Sachs ( GS ) had a disappointing response and American Express ( AXP ) failed to rouse the buyers. 
There is still hope that Alphabet ( GOOGL ) will help turn the mood positive again when it reports on Monday night, but it was Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) that really killed the mood this past week. The company reported that it saw weak smart phone demand for its chips and that pulled the rug out from under the semiconductor sector and many technology names. 
The concern about weak phone demand gained further traction Friday when an analyst reported that its checks in China show that Apple ( AAPL ) is facing stiff competition and waning demand. 
The market took the news seriously and the largest market cap stock in the market fell over 6.7% in two days and is struggling to hold its 200-day simple moving average. 
Apple and semiconductors were not the only issue bothering the market this week. A surge in oil and commodity prices ramped up some inflationary worries and that caused a drop in bonds. Also, 30-year mortgage rates hit their highest levels in four years. 
News flow has been ugly and the better technical conditions that we saw following the Netflix report quickly eroded. While there is still support on the charts, this market needs a positive response to earnings next week to get back on track. It cannot afford to revisit the lows we saw in early April. 
The market also needs some new leadership and new themes in order to produce an uptrend. There is substantial technical overhead and the narrative is increasingly bearish. 
This is a difficult environment for stocks right now and there is not much working on the long side. Capital protection and increased patience are the way to go while the market works out its issues. 
Have a great weekend. I'll see you on Monday.
